auditFix.issue: 골아파 is not a single morpheme or noun meaning 'headache'. 고라파덕's pun decomposes as 골(이) 아파(요) 'my head hurts' — a phrase combining the noun 골 'head' with the predicate 아프다. The standalone Korean noun for headache is 두통. Tagging 골아파 as a 'root/morpheme' meaning 'headache' is a part-of-speech and morphological error.

기라스 in 마기라스 (Tyranitar), 데기라스 (Pupitar), and 애버라스 (Larvitar) is borrowed from 안기라스 — the Korean name of the kaiju Anguirus from the Godzilla franchise, which Tyranitar's line visually references. It is not a transliteration of the English suffix '-tar'. Tying the root to '-tar' obscures the kaiju reference and is etymologically wrong.

깜지 in 깜지곰 (Teddiursa) is not 'small/cute'. The 깜- root is a cognate of 검-/까만 (black/dark), making 깜지곰 a 'dark/black bear' — Teddiursa has a brown-black body and the morpheme conventionally evokes blackness (cf. 깜장, 깜깜하다). The standalone noun 깜지 is school slang for a sheet of paper written so densely it looks black. Glossing it as 'small/cute' has no Korean basis and overlaps semantically with 꼬마 (which is the actual 'small' morpheme, separately listed).

노고치 (Dunsparce) is not built from a meaningful 노고 'effort'. The Korean name is a transliteration of the Japanese ノコッチ, which itself is an anagram-style scramble of 츠치노코 (tsuchinoko, the Japanese cryptid the Pokemon is based on). There is no 'effort' morpheme in the etymology — teaching learners that 노고 means 'effort' here invites them to misparse 노고치.

쥬레곤 (Dewgong) is not built from 드래곤 'dragon'. The Korean name transliterates Japanese ジュゴン (jugong, dugong) — Dewgong is a sea-mammal Pokémon based on the dugong/seal, with no dragon motif (it is Water/Ice, not Dragon-type). The Korean string '레곤' is the dugong tail, not 드래곤. Pairing the gloss 'dragon' with 쥬레곤 will mislead learners into seeing a dragon component that isn't there.

entries.gloss: horse, 馬 (only in 날쌩마; 무우마 and 마기라스 use unrelated 마 morphemes)

auditFix.issue: The single gloss '馬 horse' fits 날쌩마 (Rapidash, 날쌘+말/馬) but is wrong for the other two cited Pokémon. 무우마 (Misdreavus) is a ghost/witch — its 마 is conventionally read as 마(魔, demon/witch; cf. 마녀), reinforced by the next-stage 무우마직 (魔+직). 마기라스 (Tyranitar) takes 마기라스 from 안기라스 (the Korean name of the Godzilla kaiju Anguirus), as already noted in the 기라스 auditFix — its 마 is not 馬 either. Lumping all three under 'horse' will misparse a ghost and a kaiju as horse-themed.

잠만보 (Snorlax) plays on 잠 'sleep' + 만보, but the morphemic punchline is the colloquial 만보 ~ 만큼/매우 'a great deal' (Snorlax sleeps and eats a great deal), reinforced by Japanese カビゴン. The literal Hanja reading 萬步 'ten thousand steps' is a real Korean compound (cf. 만보계 pedometer) but is not what 잠만보 is doing — Snorlax is famously sedentary, not a stepper. 'Countless steps' is the wrong sense.

auditFix.issue: 샤 in 샤미드 (Vaporeon) is not an onomatopoeic 'water sound'. The widely cited Korean etymology is 샤워 (shower) + 머메이드 (mermaid). 샤 is a clip of 샤워 (English-derived 'shower'), a noun, not a water-sound mimetic. The current gloss invents an onomatopoeic reading.

entries.gloss: Eevee (Pokémon proper noun, transliterated from English 'Eevee' < 'Ev' of Evolution)

auditFix.issue: 이브이 is a direct transliteration of English 'Eevee' (itself read from 'Ev' of Evolution) — Korean Wikipedia and Bulbapedia confirm it is a borrowed proper noun, not a Korean root/morpheme. The shared component across the Eeveelution naming pattern (이브이 Eevee, 에브이 Espeon) is 브이 alone, not 이브이; Espeon's 에 prefix comes from 에스퍼/ESP. So both fields of the seed entry are wrong: the part of speech 'root/morpheme' overstates productivity, and treating 이브이 as a component of 에브이 is etymologically incorrect.

senses: the productive shared component in the Eeveelution naming pattern is 브이, not 이브이

entries.gloss: (no '지목' morpheme; 꼬지모 = 꼬마 + 거짓 + 木) — entry should be split or removed

auditFix.issue: 꼬지모 (Sudowoodo) does not contain a morpheme '지목' meaning 'potted tree'. The Korean fan/wiki analysis decomposes 꼬지모 as 꼬(꼬마, small) + 지(거짓, false/lie) + 모(木 mok→mo, tree) — i.e. 'small false-tree', mirroring Japanese 嘘 (uso, lie) + 木 (ki, tree) and English pseudo-+wood. The substring 지목 is not even present (the name ends in 모, not 목), and the standalone Korean noun 지목 means 'designation/specification', not 'potted tree' (bonsai is 분재). Teaching 지목 = 'potted tree' invents both a morpheme boundary and a meaning.

Cyndaquil (브케인) and Quilava (마그케인) are fire/storm hedgehog Pokémon whose Japanese names (ヒノアラシ Hinoarashi 'fire-storm', マグマラシ Magumarashi 'magma-storm') reference 嵐 'storm'. The Korean adaptation borrows from 허리케인 'hurricane' for the 케인 element — the file already contains a separate 허리케인 entry with this analysis. Glossing 케인 as 'cane/tail' contradicts both the Japanese motif (storm) and the established Korean fan analysis. 'Cane' (지팡이) and 'tail' have no support.

코리 in 코코리 (Phanpy) does not mean 'small'. 코코리 is built from 코끼리 (elephant) — the Pokemon is explicitly an elephant calf. The 코 of 코끼리 is doubled and clipped (코+코+리). Glossing the root as 'small' is invented; if anything the morpheme means 'elephant (clip of 코끼리)'.

Neither cited Pokemon supports 'cocoon-like body'. 콘팡 (Venonat) inherits from Japanese コンパン, where コン is from 'compound (eye)' (복안) — Venonat is a compound-eye gnat, not a cocoon. 쏘콘 (Forretress) uses 콘 from English 'cone' (Pineco/pinecone). A single gloss can't cover both, but 'cocoon-like body' fits neither.

auditFix.issue: The single gloss 'sun' fits 해너츠 (Sunkern, from 해바라기 sunflower) and 해루미 (Sunflora) but is wrong for 왕눈해 (Tentacool), where 해 is a clip of 해파리 (jellyfish) — Tentacool is a jellyfish, not a sun. Lumping all three under 'sun' will mislead learners into parsing 왕눈해 as 'big-eye sun'.
